newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Nat Express JV to be used for Euro buys.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Nat Express JV to be used for Euro buys.

text.p: National Express Plc, the UK transport giant, said on Monday it planned to use its new joint venture with Norway's Schoyen Group as a vehicle for major acquisitions in Continental Europe in the years ahead.

Phil White, chief executive, told Reuters in an interview that as well as tendering for public transport contracts on the Continent the venture called "Concordia Bus" would target acquisitions in the Nordic and Baltic states and Germany. "We plan to make some fairly chunky acquisitions," he said.
Concordia will target operations which have in excess of 500 buses and which operate in urban areas, with a similar business profile to its existing UK bus operations, White said.
"Schoyen has already identifed some acquisition targets. We will aim for large operators in cities."

Asked when the first deal would be delivered through the Concordia Bus joint venture, he said: "It might well not be in 1997. But I would be disappointed if we did not have at least one underway in 1998."
White declined to say how much had been ploughed into the venture, but said it was small at this stage. He said the real spending would come once acquisition targets had been lined up.
He said the joint venture for bus deals on the continent was a blueprint for entering other sectors in the region as well.
"This JV is the way we would like to enter any market. It is very important to have local contact," he said.
The National Express and Schoyen link-up was ideal, he said, because "we have experience of privatisation in the UK and Schoyen has local knowledge".
He said the companies gelled well because they were both ambitious to expand in Europe.

Explaining the rationale for a JV as a vehicle for continental acquisitions, White told Reuters: "If you wish to venture abroad, you have to realise that the markets, trade unions and politics are all different. So you have to tap into local knowledge."
On how much National Express had set aside for buys, White remained circumspect. But he indicated it had the scope to gear up considerably.
"Look at our balance sheet and we have one of the strongest among bus operators," he said. With gearing at three percent, "we have a lot of flexibility to gear up", he added.
